citations.review_text: Enough content gets a bit repetitive tho

A fairly decent game overall, in my opinion, but one that demands a considerable amount of time and patience. The majority of side quests feel repetitive, following more or less the same formula with very little variation. The graphics are undoubtedly one of the game's strongest aspects, but other elements are just okay. Naval combat is average and nowhere near the level of *AC Black Flag*, although that's somewhat understandable.

As for the story, I feel it is unnecessarily stretched, particularly the whole Cult of Kosmos storyline, which starts to feel dragged out after a while. Overall, it's a good game with plenty to offer, but you'll need to be patient and willing to invest a substantial amount of time to truly enjoy it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the world of Ancient Greece as visually impressive and expansive, featuring detailed landscapes, architecture, and exploration across islands.

citations.review_text:
Assassin's Creed Odyssey is an incredible open-world RPG that takes players into the beautiful world of Ancient Greece. One of the strongest aspects of the game is its massive open world, filled with breathtaking landscapes, historical locations, ancient temples, beautiful islands, and impressive architecture. The attention to environmental detail makes exploring the world an experience of its own.

The character design is another major highlight. Alexios and Kassandra both have distinctive personalities, well-designed appearances, and impressive character animations. Their facial expressions, dialogue delivery, and interactions help bring the story to life. The supporting characters are also memorable, with different personalities and motivations that make the world feel more alive.

The animation quality deserves special appreciation. Combat animations are fluid and satisfying, with a variety of fighting styles, weapon movements, dodges, and special abilities. The cinematic presentation during important story moments adds another layer of immersion. Whether exploring ancient cities, fighting enemies, or travelling across the Greek islands, the animations help maintain the game's visual appeal.

The combat system offers plenty of freedom. Players can experiment with different weapons, abilities, armour sets, and playstyles. The naval combat is another enjoyable feature, allowing players to explore the Mediterranean Sea and participate in ship battles. Upgrading the ship and discovering new locations adds more depth to the experience.

The soundtrack and atmosphere are also outstanding. The music complements the Greek setting beautifully, while the environmental sounds make exploration feel more immersive. Watching the sunset over the sea or exploring ancient ruins can be just as enjoyable as completing missions.

Final Verdict: Assassin's Creed Odyssey is a remarkable adventure with beautiful world-building, memorable characters, satisfying combat, and im…

Assassin’s Creed Odyssey delivers an incredible experience from beginning to end. Ancient Greece is breathtaking, the world is rich with history and mythology, and the freedom to explore makes every adventure feel worthwhile. The story is engaging, the characters are memorable, and the DLCs add even more depth to an already fantastic experience.

Whether exploring the Greek world, uncovering ancient secrets, or facing its mythical challenges, Odyssey is a game that truly makes you feel part of its world.

I bought this game on sale for 15 euros (specifically the deluxe version.) I have to say, beyond all beliefs, this is an extraordinary game with a wide map to explore and various enemies to defeat. One thing that also stood out to me were the amazing graphics and scenery, while the representation of Ancient Greece was also superb. I recommend this game to anyone who wants to have a unique gaming experience.
Genuinely enjoyed the beautiful greek world on my ultrawide monitor, it looks stunning , a literal treat to the eyes

This is my favorite Assassins Creed game, ancient Greece is lovingly recreated, the characters and voice acting are great. Think of this game as more of an action rpg set during the Peloponnesian War instead of a strictly assassins creed game, but wow, it still holds up to to when it released back in 2019. Players have the option of playing Kassandra or Alexios, I prefer Kassandra's vocal range so I would recommend playing as her. Naval battles make a return, commanding a bireme, sailing the Aegean, listening to Greek sea shanties, and cleaving enemy ships in half is honestly one of the most satisfying experience I have had in gaming in a while.

citations.review_text: Game starts off quite interesting and fun but becomes very repetitive after a while. Playing this game reminds me of my previous experience with Assassin Creed 1. Game starts off very interesting and cool, but after a few hours, becomes very repetitive, and have to struggle to continue playing (due to the repetitive nature). Overall, combat lacks depth and assassination lacks variety.
It is fun but the game is bloated and the gameplay becomes repetitive quickly.

After playing over 100 hours, completing every quest, including both DLCs and unlocking all the achievements, here’s my honest opinion.

Odyssey is a breathtaking journey through ambition, betrayal and fractured loyalties. Ancient Greece is mesmerising w/ exquisite environmental detail that constantly made me stop to admire the scenery. This game is gorgeous as hell.

The RPG systems are excellent and combat is fluid, satisfyin and addictive. The dialogue, character interactions and expressive movements create extraordinary immersion, And kicking someone off a cliff? Pure disrespect, lmao.

But the quests become repetitive, sometimes demanding considerable time for an underwhelming payoff. “Was that seriouslyy it?” sums up a few of them. Some characters also have conspicuously similar faces, I occasionally couldn’t tell who was who, lol.

My biggest criticism is how the sheer abundance of side quests overshadows the main narrative. After so many diversions, I’d forget what was happening in the central story. It deserved greater prominence, stronger continuity and more sustained emotional momentum. Ik Ik repetition is part of the AC formula, but story wise, I’d say Odyssey is decent, though nothing exceptional.

Personally, I found both DLCs better than the main storyline. Their compelling narratives and memorable moments left a deeper impression, making them the highlight of my experience. No cap!

Despite the repetition, Odyssey’s world, combat and atmosphere kept drawing me back. Imo, it’s the 3rd best AC I’ve played so far. 

7/10
It feels very different from the older Assassin's Creed games. You play more like a warrior than an assassin, and the quests get boring and repetitive.
One of the better ACs. Huge world with the beautiful atmosphere being the focal selling point. Ship combat is fun, but less so than black flag. Tons of content although most of it is copy paste slop.

Ancient Greece is beautiful and exploring its islands by land and sea is a big part of what makes this game fun. I also liked the combat and the different builds you can create. However, the game is quite long and the constant clearing of camps and completing similar quests can get tiring. It doesn't feel like a classic AC game, but as an open-world RPG, it's a pretty solid experience. Overall a 7.9/10 game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks traditional stealth mechanics and feels more like an action RPG or warrior game than a classic Assassin's Creed title.

citations.review_text: Assassin's Creed Odyssey is very fun and the main story is pretty good. This is a pretty decent RPG game, but a terrible Assassin's Creed game. The stealth is very basic and a little janky at times when combined with the parkour system in this, which is a huge step down from the classic Assassin's Creed games. The fun parts are in the combat both on land and sea. I like how the different weapon types feel unique from each other, the abilities you unlock actually are useful while not being op, and how the game can genuinely be difficult at times without keeping you stuck at one part of the game for two hours straight (Except that one hog boss fight, fuck that pig). The game isn't too grindy compared to other RPG games, all you have to do is do some side quests alongside the main story and you should be the appropriate level for most of the time. And once you do get to the higher levels, you really do start to feel much more powerful. The game itself also looks great and I love the customization (thank god for transmog). Although I must say, a lot of the acting in this game is horrendous. Some actors are actually pretty good like Alexios, but many of the side characters feel like you just started watching a Tubi movie. If you're looking for a good Assassin's Creed game, then this one isn't it and you should play something like Black Flag or the Ezio Collection. But if you're looking for a good RPG game or just really like this period of Ancient Greece (like me), then this game might be worth your time.

This was a TERRIBLE assassin's creed game. Stealth just doesn't mean anything and isn't rewarding unless your five levels above every NPC, but they all scale to you. I just considering myself playing as Odysseus from the odyssey and it honestly was fun. The world is pretty damn good looking, and I kept wanting to explore for the first 30 hours or so. It got repetetive, but by that point I was able to just finish the main story and finish. For a few bucks, this is a great game. There's easily 200 hours of content, the only issue is that not a lot would consider it good content. 
7/10
It feels very different from the older Assassin's Creed games. You play more like a warrior than an assassin, and the quests get boring and repetitive.
Ignore the AC faithfuls who dog on the newer games style. This is an excellent rpg, missing a lot of the Assassins creed DNA but incredible regardless.
terrible ac game, W rpg game u will enjoy it if u dont play it like an ac game

claims.claim: Reviewers criticize the inclusion of microtransactions and in-game cash shops in a full-priced single-player game.

citations.review_text: IMO the best AC game thus far, followed closely by Black Flag, even though this one came out a few years ago now. Played mostly on PS4 when it first came out so I actually have more like 200hrs in it. Obviously there are both good and bad things, most of the bad things though are simply the franchise selling cosmetics for WAY too much, even years after it came out, and also the fact that you need DLC's to actually finish the full story. If you don't you're kinda left on a cliffhanger and it is unfortunate to get to that and just be disappointed that you've gotta spend another $50 to be satisfied with the ending. Of course this is an AC game so the gameplay itself is largely rinse and repeat from all the other more recent games, but if you've played them before you're gonna be prepared for that. But I will say the combat is way better than it was in previous games, seems like they just finetuned the combat from Origins. Whenever I get a new AC game I know what im gonna get gameplay wise, but it's the stories that make me, and many others, always come back for more. As someone who enjoys learning about history, the series itself is really great in that aspect. They truly do make an effort to be as realistic as possible when it comes to various peoples/societies and its clear that they do their research in many areas. Obviously that does not include all the mythology stuff that they're getting more and more into lately. This game in particular feels more like the devs wanted to show how ancient Greeks genuinely believed the world around them worked, instead of just throwing in a bunch of mythology stuff for funsies. I might be biased though because Ancient Greece is one of my favorite areas of history to study so the premise is right up my alley anyways. Also I REALLY liked how you could choose who to play, it makes things more interesting for sure. Additionally, I loved the incorporation of Ithaca from Homer's The Iliad (aka The Odyssey), that classic is so fascinatin…

Exploration & Graphics: 10/10. The Ancient Greece atmosphere is incredible.
Missions: Typical Ubisoft. 80% of the game is the usual repetitive loop of "go there, kill that, steal this, free them."
Combat: Flashy and fun, especially using the god-like abilities, but enemies can be massive damage sponges if your gear isn't maxed out.
Story: Pretty good! I'm no expert, but it kept me engaged.
Verdict: Despite the classic Ubisoft grind, I genuinely liked the game. Overall, a thumbs up.

Side Note: I absolutely hate the microtransactions. Shoving an in-game cash shop and XP boosts into a full-priced, single-player game is a terrible practice.

My love for ancient Greece and lack of experience with other AC games made this a 9/10 for me. 

The story and the map is huge, all the mercenaries and the amount of side missions can take as long as you'd like it to take. I got sidetracked so haven't finished the game yet, but that means I'll spend longer in the ancient Greece.

claims.claim: The open-world map is exceptionally large and detailed, featuring Ancient Greek settings, historical landmarks, and a wide variety of side quests and points of interest.

citations.review_text:
So, I’ve finally played this game Assassin's Creed Odyssey. In my opinion, it’s the best Assassin's Creed game until now. I used to struggle to choose between AC III Remastered and AC Unity, but now I know for sure which one is my favorite.
  I have never experienced a map this detailed and beautiful, filled with so many NPCs, each with unique dialogue and animations. It’s also the longest story mode/open world game I have ever played.
To complete everything—the entire map, the main story, side quests, and the DLCs—it takes about 150 hours.
  The story is so good that I don't have words for it, also the Legacy of the First Blade DLC, in particular, left me feeling quite sad due to all the drama that happend to Kassandra , all she wanted was peace but the Greel world , woundn't let this happend.
  I definitely plan to revisit AC Origins and continue on to AC Valhalla.
The gameplay can be a bit challenging at first until you get used with it, but it becomes fairly easy once you master the combat. In my opinion, the mercenaries are the most annoying part because they’re constantly hunting you down. If your "wanted" reach level 5, it’s very difficult to shake them off unless you pay them off. The game features a huge variety of legendary, unique weapons and armor sets, as well as various skills. Perhaps the coolest feature is the list of cultists you have to track down and eliminate every single one, which will keep you busy and challenged throughout the entire game.

This is the Assassin's Creed I've been waiting for.
The world of Ancient Greece is beautiful and enormous. The attention to detail and historical accuracy? Amazing! (I've even watched YouTube videos where historians discussed what Ubisoft got right and what they got wrong in AC Odyssey.)
You feel like a time traveller witnessing one of the most fascinating periods in human history. Yeah, there are some supernatural elements, aliens, and DNA doesn't actually contain the memories of your ancestors, but that's okay. It's just a video game.
Alexios and Kassandra are charismatic, fun and relatable characters. They even remind me of Ezio — the best character in the AC universe.
The map offers a huge variety of things to do: side quests, collectibles, forts to capture, battles for territory, sailing your ship or simply getting lost and enjoying the view.
For some people, that's too much. For me? Well, I wanted more!
The DLCs are fun, but they're not as grounded as the base game. If that's not your cup of tea, just stick to the main game.
I've spent 175.6 hours in this game, left no stone unturned, completed almost everything and... in the end, I was genuinely sad that the journey had come to an end.

I've always said that Ubisoft knows how to build worlds, not games. And if there's one game that perfectly demonstrates both sides of that statement, it's this one.

Ancient Greece is absolutely mesmerizing. The islands, the architecture, the historical landmarks, the ancient writings, the mythology, and the sheer richness of the world are nothing short of extraordinary. Ubisoft has this incredible ability to recreate historical settings that make you genuinely want to explore them, not necessarily because there's a quest marker telling you to, but because you're curious about what's waiting beyond the next mountain or across the sea.

And Odyssey might be one of their finest achievements in that regard.

I spent countless hours sailing between islands, wandering through ancient cities, exploring ruins, discovering secrets, and immersing myself in Greek history and mythology. Every region felt like another opportunity to discover something fascinating. I was so captivated by this world that I ended up completing 100% of the game, something I rarely bother doing.

The mythology deserves special praise. Gods, legendary creatures, ancient mysteries, and the constant blending of history with myth made the experience endlessly fascinating. And the power fantasy? Absolutely ridiculous, in the best possible way. By the end, you're less of an Assassin and more of a Greek demigod casually walking around and ruining everyone's day. I loved that.

I played as Kassandra, and she was a fantastic protagonist. Charismatic, entertaining, and genuinely fun to inhabit throughout such an enormous adventure. The story itself was decent, nothing particularly groundbreaking, but it did its job and gave me enough reason to keep going.

Unfortunately, this is also where my usual Ubisoft criticism comes in.

The gameplay loop starts out genuinely enjoyable. The combat, abilities, progression, exploration, and activities all feel satisfying initially. But after dozens upon dozens of hours, t…

Horas jugadas al momento del análisis: 214h

Completado: Historia principal, Culto de Kosmos, sellado mítico y DLC Legacy of the First Blade.

Assassin's Creed Odyssey es un viaje monumental. Si buscas un juego lineal o corto, este no es tu lugar; pero si buscas un action-RPG inmersivo donde perderte semanas explorando la Antigua Grecia, ofrece contenido de sobra para justificar cada centavo.

Lo mejor:

Ambientación y escala: Visualmente Grecia es espectacular; navegar entre islas y explorar ruinas históricas nunca cansa.

Combate y builds: Gran variedad de estilos. Armar configuraciones enfocadas en daño de Asesino, críticos y habilidades como Hero Strike o disparos de francotirador con el arco se siente sumamente gratificante.

El árbol del Culto: La mecánica de investigar pistas y cazar a los miembros del Culto de Kosmos uno a uno por todo el mapa es uno de los mejores sistemas que ha tenido la saga.

Conexión de lore: El DLC Legacy of the First Blade cierra con un broche de oro que sirve como la antesala perfecta para Assassin's Creed Origins.

Puntos a tener en cuenta:

El mapa es gigantesco y por momentos puede sentirse abrumador si eres completista. Es fácil dispersarse con misiones secundarias repetitivas si no te enfocas en la historia y los objetivos clave.

Requiere optimizar bien configuraciones en PC y clientes de arranque para evitar cuellos de botella en pantallas de carga.

Veredicto:

Un juego enorme, divertido y con un ciclo de combate adictivo. Cerrar la historia de Kassandra tras más de 200 horas deja una satisfacción tremenda. Totalmente recomendado. 9/10

claims.claim: Combat involves managing adrenaline to execute special abilities and can feel repetitive or sponge-like against bosses after extended play.

citations.review_text: An AC game that focuses on a strong character in a Greek family tragedy without the usual assassins. The ancestors and bloodline are still the main story, but this time you have more self-determination to earn coins and loot by doing jobs in the fabulous Greek world. Messenger, courier, hunter, burglary, piracy, sabotage, mercenary and naturally send someone to Hades. Sometimes you only get directions to an island or region and get to find the quest marker on your own. You are rewarded with varied loot to build up to 5 loadouts. Every item of clothing and weapon has two or three special properties and at a blacksmith you can choose one more. The combat and abilities are easy to use. I started collecting gear with critical change/damage and after gaining abilities, gear that increased adrenaline, because that’s the resource the abilities consume.

I haven't played Origins, but after 100% achievement (DLC required) I can say that this is the best AC but not AC game I've ever played next to OG Black Flag. It is bloated, grindy, repetitive, and very long. But it is fun.

-Purposefully grindy just to sell you their perma XP and money boost.
-Abilities are substituted for tools from previous games. Some abilities are just mandatory like Second Wind and Battlecry of Ares while some are just useless or situational like Beast Master and Call to Arms.
-There are bound to be bugs and I encountered plenty.
-With how grindy and expensive it is to upgrade, the game incentivize you to steal.
-Combat is drastically changed. But every combat is about the same, even all the bosses. Melee combat is just button mashing light attack, occasionally use heavy attack, use abilities when off cooldown, use overpower attack when you have the adrenaline, dodge only on red attacks, and dodge/parry white attacks. Ranged combat is similar to melee but keeping distance and barrage enemies with arrows.
-Bounty hunter system is slightly like the Nemesis system and is the generic crime/wanted system. You can pay off your Wanted status, but there is no reason to later in the game when you can easily kill the BHunters and they're just walking resources.
-The game is an RPG so naturally the game will level gate you with high level enemies that can easily kill you. But if you're exploring or not rushing the game, it isn't an issue.
-The highest difficulty isn't even hard if you got the right gears with engraves to tank or do a lot of damage. But not recommended for early game.
-The level scaling setting is nice to have but feels mandatory to have since it also effect gear loot level, reduce upgrade resources on them, and have more value for selling or dismantling.
-Eagle vision is changed to being literal. You control Ikaros allows you to view everything from bird's POV and tells you everything from point of interest, tag enemies, chests, objectiv…
